title: 2017 Barker Legal Studies Trial
notes: The answer sheet in the PDF is blank. The marking-guidelines pages do not include a Section I answer key. The bundled multiple-choice questions contain no stimulus figures or diagrams.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a non-government organisation which promotes human rights?

options.C: The World Trade Organisation
options.D: The International Criminal Court

questions.answerNote: World Vision is a non-government organisation; The other options are intergovernmental or judicial bodies.

questions.stem: Which purpose of punishment is achieved by fining a speeding driver?

options.C: General deterrence
options.D: Specific deterrence

questions.answerNote: Specific deterrence: the fine is imposed on this driver to discourage that driver from reoffending. General deterrence (C) is also plausible because fines send a message to other drivers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of situational crime prevention?

options.C: Providing scholarships for disadvantaged children
options.D: Reducing the number of police officers patrolling during the daytime

questions.answerNote: Anti-graffiti paint changes the environment to reduce opportunities for offending.

questions.stem: Who of the following is an accessory before the fact?

options.A: A person who robs a bank
options.B: A person who agreed with the plan to rob the bank
options.C: A person who advises another person how to rob a bank
options.D: A person who hides the money after the bank has been robbed

questions.answerNote: An accessory before the fact assists or encourages the offence before it occurs; Advising the offender fits this role.

questions.stem: Which of the following was the first internationally recognised human right?

options.C: Universal education
options.D: Freedom from slavery

questions.answerNote: The prohibition of slavery was recognised in early international instruments, including the 1926 Slavery Convention.

questions.stem:
A person is convicted of a minor crime in the local court. He is required to report to the police station once a week.

What type of penalty does this represent?

options.C: Imprisonment
options.D: Criminal infringement notice

questions.answerNote: A bond may impose conditions such as reporting to police; The person is not imprisoned.

questions.stem:
A person is accused of smuggling cocaine from Bangkok to Melbourne.

What type of crime has he committed?

options.C: A crime against the sovereign
options.D: A crime against the international community

questions.answerNote: The alleged drug smuggling crosses national borders, making it transnational crime.

questions.stem: What is it called when the police arrest someone and formally accuse them of a crime?

options.C: Indictment
options.D: Conviction

questions.answerNote: Police formally accuse a person by charging them; Indictment is a later formal accusation for certain proceedings.

questions.stem:
A young person is 15 when he is caught shoplifting.

Which of the following is NOT an alternative to court available to him?

options.C: Circle sentencing
options.D: Youth justice conferencing

questions.answerNote: Circle sentencing is a sentencing process in court (mainly for Aboriginal offenders), not an alternative to court like a warning, caution or youth justice conference.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true once a prisoner has served his minimum sentence?

options.C: He can request another sentencing hearing.
options.D: He will be reclassified as a minimum security prisoner.

questions.answerNote: Serving the non-parole period makes the prisoner eligible to apply for parole; Release is not automatic.

questions.stem: How does the division of powers protect human rights in Australia?

options.A: By ensuring the rule of law is maintained
options.B: By giving different responsibilities to the legislature, executive and judiciary
options.C: By allowing both state and federal governments to pass laws enforcing human rights
options.D: By allowing citizens to appeal to the High Court if they believe legislation violates human rights

questions.answerNote: The division of powers between Commonwealth and state governments allows both levels to legislate in areas affecting human rights.

questions.stem: How is the link between the behaviour of an accused and the injury to a victim best described?

options.C: Actus reus
options.D: Recklessness

questions.answerNote: Causation is the connection between the accused’s conduct and the resulting injury.

questions.stem:
Evidence is seized during a police search of a property.

Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: The evidence is admissible if the police had a warrant.
options.B: Police do not have the power to seize evidence from properties.
options.C: The evidence is admissible if it is in the public interest to seize it.
options.D: The evidence is only admissible if the suspect is present during the search.

questions.answerNote: A warrant authorises search and seizure; The other options are not general conditions. Public-interest admissibility (C) is a weaker second option under Evidence Act s138.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about a criminal trial in NSW?

options.A: The accused must present a defence.
options.B: All witnesses must be cross examined.
options.C: The judge rules on the admissibility of evidence.
options.D: The judge instructs the jury about which evidence it should believe.

questions.answerNote: The judge determines legal questions, including admissibility of evidence; Jurors assess the facts.

questions.stem:
A salesperson sells alcohol to a 16 year old without an ID.

Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: In this case, the burden of proof shifts to the defendant.
options.B: The prosecution has to prove its case on the balance of probabilities.
options.C: The prosecution has to prove that the salesperson knew that the buyer was 16.
options.D: The prosecution does not have to prove that the salesperson knew that the buyer was 16.

questions.answerNote: This is a strict liability offence, so the prosecution need not prove the salesperson knew the buyer’s age.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about a jury’s verdict?

options.A: A jury must return a unanimous verdict.
options.B: Only ten of the twelve jurors have to agree with the verdict.
options.C: A jury can return a majority verdict after eight hours of deliberation.
options.D: A judge must direct that a majority verdict is possible before the jury retires.

questions.answerNote: NSW permits a majority verdict after the prescribed deliberation period, which is generally eight hours.

questions.stem:
An accused argues at his hearing that he was provoked when he assaulted the victim.

How is this evidence relevant?

options.A: The magistrate can reduce the charge.
options.B: The evidence of provocation is only relevant in sentencing.
options.C: The defence must prove the victim provoked the accused.
options.D: If successful, the evidence of provocation will lead to an acquittal.

questions.answerNote: Provocation is a partial defence to murder, not assault; For assault it may be relevant as a mitigating sentencing factor.

questions.stem: Which of the following rights is best protected in Australia by the common law?

options.C: Freedom of association
options.D: The right to legal representation

questions.answerNote: Common law recognises procedural protections including access to legal representation; The other rights rely more directly on legislation or constitutional protection.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the role of regional intergovernmental organisations in the promotion and enforcement of human rights?

options.A: They encourage victims to take action.
options.B: They create international human rights law.
options.C: They raise awareness of human rights issues.
options.D: They take action to remedy breaches of human rights.

questions.answerNote: Regional systems can provide mechanisms and institutions that investigate and remedy human rights breaches.

questions.stem:
An accused pleads guilty, and gives evidence against her co-conspirators.

Which of the following best describes the key factor the judge will consider in sentencing?

options.A: She has saved the court time, which is a mitigating factor.
options.B: She gave evidence as a witness, which is an aggravating factor.
options.C: She is an accessory after the fact, which is an aggravating factor.
options.D: She is a principal in the first degree, which is a mitigating factor.

questions.answerNote: A guilty plea can reduce the burden on the court and is a mitigating sentencing consideration.
